title: Tampa's Big Week, Edmonton's Hot Finishing, and a Wild Overtime Night
dek: Tampa Bay's top line piled up points, Nashville stayed perfect, and a few of the league's loudest stories came with asterisks.
text:
## The week's best story: Tampa's top line, and a goalie in Nashville

Tampa Bay played four games and left with the league's top scoring line. Jake Guentzel had 9 points (3 goals, 6 assists), Nikita Kucherov had 8 (4 goals, 4 assists), John Carlson had 8 on one goal and seven assists, and Brandon Hagel scored 5 goals. Kucherov also had a hat trick on Nov. 11. Guentzel and Kucherov each had 1.7 expected goals, a measure of the quality of their chances, so the goals were not far out of line with the looks. Hagel's five goals came on 2.9 expected, so some finishing luck is in there.

Nashville went 4-0-0 and is now on a seven-game winning streak. The chances only half back it: the Predators have 51 percent of the expected goals in that run. The reason is Juuse Saros, our goalie of the week. He faced 98 shots over three games, allowed 3 goals, and posted a .969 save percentage. Goals saved above expected, which compares what a goalie stopped with what an average goalie would have, came to 5.8. Across the streak, Nashville's goaltending has saved 10.9 goals above expected.

## Who the league is talking about

Matvei Michkov led the chatter with 77 headlines from 33 outlets in five days. The Hockey News asked whether the Flyers give him enough playing time. PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor posted that Rick Tocchet "dismissed the idea that he was forced by mgmt into giving Matvei Michkov more mins Wed," but that Tocchet's version "doesn't tell the whole story." We can't say who is right from our data, only that the argument is loud.

Nick Cousins of Ottawa drew 56 headlines after a hit by Chychrun. Markerzone ran "Travis Green confirms scary Nick Cousins update," and that's all we know from the coverage.

Connor Hellebuyck's return to Winnipeg with New Jersey brought Yahoo's "Craig Carton defends Devils' decision to sit Connor Hellebuyck for his return to Winnipeg." Yahoo also reported he was greeted with vulgar chants. The Hockey News' Mike Fink posted that he was in the net for the Devils two days later.

Connor McDavid, meanwhile, is on a 20-game point streak (11 goals, 38 assists), and Oilers Nation reported he is the runaway Hart favourite in its awards poll. Our numbers agree he's producing, but note below that Edmonton's finishing looks hot.

## The games

The game of the week was Nov. 7, when New Jersey beat the Islanders 5-4 in overtime, with Jack Hughes as the star. The Devils had 5.45 expected goals to 3.24 and deserved to win 80 percent of the time. That figure is the share of simulated replays of every shot in which they win.

The biggest steal went the other way. Edmonton beat the Rangers 3-1 on Nov. 9 with Leon Draisaitl as the star, but the Rangers had 3.6 expected goals to 1.96, and Edmonton deserved to win only 15 percent of the time. Tampa Bay's 4-3 overtime win over Minnesota on Nov. 7 was one-sided on chances: 4.12 expected goals to 1.96.

The week's unlikeliest goals were Jack St. Ivany's snap shot for Washington against Florida (a 0.3 percent chance), Darren Raddysh's slap shot for Toronto (0.9 percent) and Devon Toews's snap shot for Colorado (1.3 percent), both in the Nov. 10 game. Hat tricks came from Matt Boldy, Kucherov and Cutter Gauthier.

## Trending up, trending down

Carolina went 2-0-0 and outscored opponents 13-3 with 64 percent of the expected goals. Winnipeg went 3-0-0 with 57 percent and has won five straight, outscoring teams 27-14 with 60 percent of the expected goals. The chances back that run.

Vancouver is winless in seven (0-7-0), outscored 30-14, with 43 percent of the expected goals, and sits last at 3-17-1. Detroit (winless in five) and Toronto (winless in five, outscored 22-9) also look as bad as they've played. Minnesota has points in ten straight and Montreal in twelve straight.

## Milestones and streaks

Carlson and Roman Josi each reached 800 career points. Taylor Hall played his 1,000th NHL game. Brayden Point hit 700 career points, and Guentzel played his 700th game. Granlund has a seven-game point streak for Anaheim, Mark Scheifele has a five-game streak with 4 goals and 6 assists, and Draisaitl has a seven-game streak.

## Who's due to swing

Edmonton's finishing is the number to watch. Evan Bouchard has 11 goals on 3.9 expected, Draisaitl 18 on 11.8, and McDavid 11 on 7.8. The chances are real, but those finishing rates rarely last. On the other side, Pavel Dorofeyev has 6 goals on 9.5 expected and J.T. Miller 4 on 7.4, both for the Rangers, who should see more goals if the looks keep coming.
